reviews.summary: Unlike the generic top results (idea lists with no timing), it starts from when they find out and adds a seven-day clue schedule, a what-to-tell-them-to-pack table and the passport/ESTA/ETA check. Polish: 'sunscreen' and 'warm hat' for US readers; 'holiday' in a heading.

Every Pack Your Bags, Passport, scheduling and link claim checked against the code. Fixes: 'sun cream'/'woolly hat' are British, say 'sunscreen'/'warm hat'; the Spanish lead lacked the English lead's new 'weekend away or holiday abroad'. Polish: the FAQ hides the booking 'inside' sunscreen, say 'turn the booking into something they open … as a hint'; a photo puzzle may have no name on it.

Fixes: the UK phrase 'surprise holiday reveal' (590 a month, we sit near 3) belongs in the English lead; the English lacks the not-yet-booked case the Spanish FAQ covers and the 'gift a surprise vacation' results answer. Polish: smoother description, keyword headings, an exploding box, an answer to '¿Dónde puedo regalar viajes sorpresa?'.

applied: EN: 'sunscreen and flip-flops … a warm hat' in the body and FAQ
EN lead: 'Below are surprise trip and holiday reveal ideas for every timing, for a weekend away or a holiday abroad'
ES lead: «para una escapada o unas vacaciones fuera» (shorter than the reviewer's wording: the test caps the lead at 90 words)

EN FAQ on clever ways to give a trip: opens 'Turn the booking into something they open … as a hint' and ends with the unbooked case ('We're going to Lisbon. You choose when.' Only promise a hotel or a flight you've already paid for); ES FAQ opens «Convierte la reserva en algo que tenga que abrir … como pista»
Puzzle, both languages: 'the pieces that give it away (the name, or the landmark)'
rejected: Search polish, a '¿Dónde puedo regalar viajes sorpresa?' answer: it would mean pointing at mystery-trip agencies, and posts name other makers only in comparison posts
Search polish, an exploding box and keyword-stuffed headings: not needed for the search, and every new line is more for the next panel to clear

reviews.summary: It sorts reveals by how long you can keep the secret and handles the packing and documents that list-style pages skip; the 'You choose when' card is the line to screenshot. Polish only: 'the last idea is the one for you', 'already booked' for 'paid for'.

Both round-1 fixes and the polish are in and correct in both languages, every template and scheduling claim checks against the code, and the new list items don't fall into a pattern. Polish: «en el extranjero» for «fuera» if words free up.

The top results are mostly Disney and family reveal lists; this picks the reveal by how much notice they need, then covers the packing and paperwork that make a surprise trip go wrong, and now speaks the UK 'holiday' wording and the unbooked case. Polish: a QR-code card, a balloon or exploding box.
